title: Pythagorean theorem
statement: In Euclidean geometry, a right triangle with leg lengths a and b and hypotenuse length c satisfies a squared plus b squared equals c squared.
limitations: The statement assumes Euclidean geometry and a right angle; other geometries require different relations.

title: Derivative as a limit
statement: The derivative of a function at a point is the limit, when it exists, of the change in the function divided by the corresponding change in its input as that input change approaches zero.
limitations: The definition requires a specified domain and notion of limit; not every function is differentiable.

title: Bayes theorem
statement: For events with a nonzero conditioning probability, Bayes theorem relates a conditional probability to the reverse conditional probability multiplied by the prior and divided by the evidence probability.
limitations: The theorem is exact, but an application is only as sound as its event model and probability assignments.

title: Algorithm
statement: An algorithm is a finite, well-defined procedure that transforms allowed inputs into outputs through an ordered set of effective steps.
limitations: Some computational models allow nonterminating processes, so termination must be stated as part of the specific contract.

title: Binary search
statement: Binary search locates a target in an ordered search space by repeatedly comparing with a midpoint and discarding the half that cannot contain the target.
limitations: Correctness requires a maintained ordering invariant and a comparison relation compatible with that order.

title: Graph data structure
statement: A graph represents entities as vertices and relationships as edges; direction, labels, weights, and multiplicity are additional properties selected by the graph model.
limitations: Graph semantics come from the declared model; an edge alone does not establish causation.

title: Quantum superposition
statement: A quantum state may be represented as a linear combination of allowed basis states, and measurement probabilities depend on the amplitudes in that state representation.
limitations: Superposition is a mathematical and experimentally supported feature of quantum theory, not a claim that a macroscopic object literally has every classical property at once.

title: Invariant speed of light in special relativity
statement: Special relativity models inertial observers using transformations that preserve the same vacuum light speed and the spacetime interval.
limitations: The statement concerns local inertial frames and does not by itself describe gravity or accelerated coordinate systems.

title: First law of thermodynamics
statement: For a specified system, change in internal energy is accounted for by energy transferred as heat and work, subject to the chosen sign convention.
limitations: The system boundary and sign convention must be declared before applying the energy balance.

title: Stellar nuclear fusion
statement: Main-sequence stars produce outward energy primarily through nuclear fusion in their cores, where light nuclei are converted into more tightly bound nuclei.
limitations: Dominant reaction chains and stellar structure depend on stellar mass, composition, and evolutionary stage.

title: Cosmic expansion
statement: Modern cosmology models the large-scale universe with a time-dependent scale factor, supported in part by the systematic redshift-distance relation of distant galaxies.
limitations: Local gravitationally bound systems do not simply expand with the cosmological scale factor, and parameter estimates carry observational uncertainty.

title: Exoplanet transit method
statement: The transit method detects periodic decreases in a star's measured brightness when an orbiting body crosses the stellar disk from the observer's line of sight.
limitations: Transit signals require geometric alignment and must be separated from stellar variability and other false positives.

title: Chemical element and atomic number
statement: A chemical element is identified by the number of protons in its atomic nuclei, called the atomic number; isotopes of one element differ in neutron count.
limitations: Ionization changes electron count, not elemental identity; nuclear reactions can change the atomic number.

title: Dynamic chemical equilibrium
statement: At dynamic equilibrium, forward and reverse processes continue while their rates are equal, so macroscopic composition remains constant under fixed conditions.
limitations: Changing temperature, pressure, or composition can shift the equilibrium state.

title: Structure-property relationship in materials
statement: A material's observable properties depend not only on chemical composition but also on structure across electronic, atomic, microstructural, and macroscopic scales.
limitations: The relevant structural scale and measurement conditions vary with the property under study.
